reasons: The code's ADU status is special exception (27-301.2B(1), 27-301.2B(2)(d))
An accessory dwelling unit is a special exception (Zoning Hearing Board) in RI, MI, NC, CD and MG. It is not listed in TC or I (27-301.2B(1) table)
One ADU, accessory to a single-family dwelling: a detached house, a twin or a townhouse (27-301.2B(2)(d)1))
The owner of the lot must live in one of the two dwellings 'in perpetuity' (27-301.2B(2)(d)2))

Inside the house: at most 25% of the existing house's habitable floor area. As an addition: an increase of at most 25% of that area. In an accessory building: the accessory building limits, a building FOOTPRINT at most two thirds of the house's footprint, not two thirds of its floor area (27-301.2B(2)(d)6), 27-404.2B(1))

An accessory building may be at most two stories or two thirds of the actual house height, whichever is less (20 ft for a 30 ft house, 23 ft only for a 35 ft house). With a one-story house it may not be taller than the house. No more than two accessory buildings on a lot (27-404.2B(2), (3))
At most one bedroom (27-301.2B(2)(d)7))
A detached ADU may not be in the required front yard. Its own entrance, not in the front facade of the house (27-301.2B(2)(d)4), 5))

The ADU meets the setback and coverage rules of the district for its type. In the RI chart an accessory building is 8 ft from the rear line and 5 ft from the side, or attached. The detached house is 25 ft rear, 5 ft side, 80% impervious (27-301.2B(2)(d)3), Attachment 1)
Public electric, water and sewer, connected to the house's existing systems (27-301.2B(2)(d)11))

Parking: 1 space for the ADU ('Accessory dwelling unit 1 space'), 3 in all with a detached house or townhouse. The ADU may not remove any existing off-street space. The Borough may adjust the minimum under 27-405.3 (27-405.2C, 27-301.2B(2)(d)10))
Registered with the Borough every year. The registration ends when the lot is sold, and the new owner may register again (27-301.2B(2)(d)8))
A concept plan to scale with the building permit application (27-301.2B(2)(d)9))
MI, NC, CD and MG allow the same residential building types as RI, and the RI standards may be modified by up to 25% to fit the streetscape (Attachment 1)
Lots under one acre take infill standards from the block: the minimum lot area is the median lot area on the block face, side yards match an adjacent lot (27-301.1A)
In RI no new building type or residential use may be introduced in a block unless the tract is at least eight acres (27-301.1D). That limits a duplex, not the ADU
Residential uses are permitted by right in TC, but TC does not list the ADU

The RI chart sets a minimum building spacing of 10 ft for single-family detached and twin houses. Whether it reaches an accessory building on the same lot is not clear, since the chart also lets accessory buildings be attached (Attachment 1)

Condition: The code's ADU status is special exception. 'The uses listed below are permitted by special exception in the zoning districts as indicated below.' The ADU row is marked in RI, MI, NC, CD and MG. (27-301.2B(1), 27-301.2B(2)(d))
Condition: 'One of the dwellings shall be occupied, in perpetuity, by the owner of the lot on which both dwellings are located.' (27-301.2B(2)(d)2))

Condition: An internal ADU is built within an existing house, an attached ADU as an addition to an existing house. Its size is measured from the house's habitable floor area before construction. (27-202, 27-301.2B(2)(d)6))
Condition: At most one bedroom. (27-301.2B(2)(d)7))

Condition: Detached ADU: the accessory building footprint is at most two thirds of the house footprint. Height at most two stories or two thirds of the house height, whichever is less, and no taller than a one-story house. At most two accessory buildings on the lot. (27-301.2B(2)(d)6)c), 27-404.2B)
Condition: A detached ADU may not be in the required front yard. An entrance separate from the house's, not in the house's front facade. (27-301.2B(2)(d)4), 5))
Condition: Public electric, water and sewer, connected to the house's existing systems. (27-301.2B(2)(d)11))
Condition: Registered with the Borough every year. The registration ends when the lot is conveyed. A concept plan to scale with the building permit application. (27-301.2B(2)(d)8), 9))
Condition: The ADU may not remove any existing off-street parking on the lot. (27-301.2B(2)(d)10))

assumptions: land cover is per lot, plus what lies inside the best spot (spot_cover). The fit itself does not steer around trees
accessory buildings of 180 sq ft or more are garages, smaller ones are sheds that could go
a new unit goes behind the front of the house when there is room
a unit is at least 12 ft on its short side and at most 3:1
assumed heights: 15 ft for 1 story, 25 ft for 2 stories
flags: steep slope or landslide when 25% or more of the lot is in the layer, flood at 10%, historic at 50% or the lot center in a district
land cover from an aerial model (NAIP 2022): not validated here, no labeled land cover in this county
front setback 21.5 ft: contextual, taken from the existing house
attached ADUs are allowed but not modeled: the internal fit stands in for them
a new unit keeps 5 ft from garages and sheds (planning clearance, closer needs a rated wall)

ground slope from USGS 3DEP 1 m DEM, project PA_17County_D24 flown 2024-04-14 to 2025-04-02, on a 3 ft grid. Reported next to the fit, which is a flat-ground test. Steep is 25 percent or more (mean under the best spot)
